record.original_question: If P and Q are Scott sober dcpos, must their product dcpo P x Q also be Scott sober? Here Scott sober means that the Scott space of the dcpo is sober.

evidence.quote: Question 4.6. Let P, Q be Scott sober dcpos. Must the product P x Q be Scott sober?
Definition 4.4. Let P be a dcpo. (1) P is said to be Scott sober if SigmaP is sober.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A directed complete partial order (dcpo) is a partially ordered set $(P,\le)$ in which every directed subset $D\subseteq P$ has a supremum $ igsqcup D$ in $P$. The Scott topology $\sigma(P)$ on a dcpo $P$ has as its open sets the subsets $U\subseteq P$ such that (i) $U$ is an upper set (if $x\in U$ and $x\le y$, then $y\in U$), and (ii) for every directed subset $D\subseteq P$ with $ igsqcup D\in U$, one has $D\cap U
e\emptyset$. The Scott space of $P$ is $\Sigma P:=(P,\sigma(P))$.

A topological space $X$ is sober if every nonempty irreducible closed subset of $X$ (i.e., a nonempty closed set that is not the union of two strictly smaller closed sets) is the closure of a unique singleton. A dcpo $P$ is called Scott sober if $\Sigma P$ is sober.

Given dcpos $P$ and $Q$, their product dcpo $P	imes Q$ is the cartesian product equipped with the coordinatewise order $(p_1,q_1)\le(p_2,q_2)\iff p_1\le p_2$ and $q_1\le q_2$, which is again a dcpo.

Question: If $P$ and $Q$ are Scott sober dcpos, must the product dcpo $P	imes Q$ be Scott sober?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint constructs two dcpos whose Scott spaces are sober but whose order product has a non-sober Scott space, thereby answering this question in the negative.

status_evidence.title: Products of two sober dcpo's need not be sober
status_evidence.snippet: Two dcpos whose Scott spaces are sober were constructed, but the Scott space of their order product is not sober, answering an open problem on the sobriety of Scott spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The product of two Scott sober dcpos need not be Scott sober.
